dailyInsight.headline: Audit global OpenClaw sessions before treating one shared key as shared agent identity
dailyInsight.insight: OpenClaw's public source now describes and exercises a boundary that matters to multi-agent operators: session.scope: "global" can share a key without merging agents' conversations, task-notification destinations, or policy identities. Before depending on that boundary, run a disposable requester-ownership smoke test across two selected agents.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The fresh change documents that queued task updates retain the recorded requester even when another agent executes the task, and that a global session key does not merge commands, skills, replies, or background notifications. Its focused test also preserves a named requester while a different agent executes an ACP child, including requester-specific sandbox behavior.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: Mistaking a global session key for one shared agent identity can associate task updates with the wrong operator or evaluate a spawn under the wrong policy. A short audit is a safer response than assuming that a shared key is itself a sufficient security or routing boundary.

actions.audience: OpenClaw operators using global session scope with more than one selected agent or agent-specific policy
actions.label: Run a requester-ownership smoke test
actions.instruction: In a disposable configuration, give two named agents different sandbox or policy settings and enable global session scope. Have agent A launch one harmless child task assigned to agent B, then confirm that the queued completion remains attributed to agent A and that agent A's policy governs the request. Keep production credentials and live channels out of this test.

receipts.title: fix: preserve agent ownership across global sessions and bindings (#133715)
receipts.supports: The public change records the ownership-preservation work and its focused routing, binding, task-delivery, sandbox, and test coverage.

receipts.title: Global-session ownership and queued task-delivery documentation
receipts.supports: It states that the global key does not merge agents' conversations and that commands, skills, replies, and task notifications retain the routed or explicitly selected agent.

receipts.title: Global requester ownership with ACP spawn sandbox modes
receipts.supports: The focused fixture uses a global requester session with a named requester and a different executing agent, preserving requester ownership and rejecting the spawn when that requester's sandbox policy forbids it.

confidence.basis: The fresh commit, contemporaneous public documentation, and focused test agree on explicit ownership under a global key and requester-aware policy evaluation. They support a reversible audit, not a claim about any live installation.

dailyInsight.limitation: These are source-level documentation and test receipts. They do not establish the behavior of a particular configuration, release, channel integration, retry path, binding migration, or external-plugin failure.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise or withdraw the call if public source or a regression shows agents sharing a global key can consume one another's queued update, route a task to an unrecorded requester, or calculate a requester-specific policy solely from the global key.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for public operational guidance or regression coverage for global sessions through reconnects, binding replacement, queued delivery, and heterogeneous agent policies.
